title: Canonical R1-A5 live teleop driven by the unmodified xr_teleoperate solver
comparability: Not comparable with runs made before the initial-head-anchor wrist re-expression or with runs whose joints came from this project's own solvers. The joint targets here are produced by third_party/xr_teleoperate_v1_6 R1_A5_ArmIK, unmodified, in a separate process after this repository removes current-head motion from the vendor wrist transport frame.

session_calibration.head_output: pitch/yaw relative to the captured orientation
session_calibration.wrist_output: vendor current-head-relative wrist pose inverted to robot-basis XR world, then expressed against the captured head position/yaw
session_calibration.lifetime: one upstream streamer process; deadman release does not reset the anchor

independence_contract.head_only_motion: changes only relative head pitch/yaw; stationary world-space controllers retain identical anchored wrist targets
independence_contract.controller_motion: changes the corresponding anchored wrist target independently of headset translation or rotation
independence_contract.scope: Quest-to-IK target generation; simulator and hardware share this producer

model.body_mode_reason: The vendor reduced model locks waist_yaw_joint, head_pitch_joint and head_yaw_joint, so the torso cannot be given to it. Head angles are mapped from the recorded head pose outside the solver.
model.hold_reason: The vendor solver assumes a rigid torso. The asset's 100 N m/rad waist actuator bends up to 22.4 deg under the arms' reaction torque, which moved the hand by up to 153 mm in a measured run for reasons unrelated to the arm solution.

solver.process: external; runs in the tv conda environment beside the Quest bridge
solver.reason_for_separate_process: CasADi and the Pinocchio 3 CasADi bindings exist only in tv; the Isaac environment has Pinocchio 2.7 without them. Upstream also ships a package named teleop that collides with this repository's.
solver.target_frame_reason: TeleVuer first emits its audited current-head-yaw-relative waist pose. The streamer reverses only that moving-head transform and applies the captured initial head position/yaw, retaining the vendor's fixed [0.15, 0, 0.45] m workspace offset and wrist convention. The vendor r1_a5.urdf gives waist_yaw_joint a zero origin, so no project-asset waist offset is added.

rate_limiting.reason: Running the vendor solver unmodified means its WeightedMovingFilter is the only smoothing in the path. A second limiter here would make this no longer the vendor's behaviour. Applied joint velocity is measured and reported under metrics.upstream_joint_stream instead.
rate_limiting.observed_basis: Replay of t007_whole_upper_body_20260823T122433Z through the streamer: joint step p95 9.03 deg, max 16.98 deg at 30 Hz, i.e. 8.9 rad/s.

invalid_if: required evidence or the resolved configuration is missing
the controlled joint order differs from the declared 12-joint arms_head order
waist_yaw or waist_roll moves while hold_uncontrolled_waist_joints is true
any applied joint vector did not come from the vendor solver
scientific_failure_if: a run is reported as vendor behaviour while anything in this repository reshaped the solved vector
joint limit clamping is systematic rather than numerical, which would mean the two assets have diverged
the achieved control rate or tracking residual does not meet a separately declared acceptance criterion
